title: the orient floor places a chartered top-level directory on the axis
intention: orient's floor places any top-level directory that carries an intention+why.json on the complexity axis from that charter, so a ref under bin/ yields a domain.
why: Measured 2026-11-13 by the orchestrator charting a4f5804c724a: _rung returns None for every ref under bin/, so floor_packet's domain is None; re-measured on akienasus: floor_packet('x in bin/cmd/proofgate') gives refs ['bin/cmd/proofgate'], domain None.
how: D1: _rung(ref, root) reads <root>/<segment>/intention+why.json for a first segment the fixed rungs do not place, returning (segment, runtime_role or node_class); floor_packet passes root. D2: red-first proof.

clauses.claim: floor_packet('x in bin/cmd/proofgate') has a non-None domain naming bin and the rung bin's charter declares
under a scratch root, a top-level directory with no intention+why.json gets no rung, and cairn/devices/<x> still reads (device)

decisions.text: D1: _rung gains root=CAIRN_ROOT; after the fixed rungs, a first segment whose <root>/<segment>/intention+why.json parses returns (segment, runtime_role or node_class); floor_packet calls _rung(r, root).
D2: one proof, one tooth per clause, binding orient at call time.

out: the fixed rungs for cairn/, skills/ and CairnCommons

measured.how: PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c floor_packet('x in bin/cmd/proofgate') on akienasus
